transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

I've been really struggling at work lately because I keep making careless mistakes and missing important details. I'm also finding it hard to stay focused and often feel really restless and fidgety, which is starting to affect my daily life.
Do you also often interrupt others, have trouble waiting your turn, or act impulsively without thinking?
I'm not really sure about that, to be honest. I haven't really noticed myself doing those things, or at least no one has pointed it out to me.
Do you also have trouble organizing tasks, following through on instructions, or losing things needed for work or daily activities?
Honestly, I don't think those are major issues for me. I'm generally pretty good at keeping track of my things, and my organization seems okay once I actually get started on a task.
Have these attention and restlessness problems been present since childhood or early adolescence, and do they happen in more than one setting like work, home, or school?

Yes, I've struggled with these issues for as long as I can remember, definitely since before I was 12 years old. It affects me everywhere—not just with keeping up at work, but also at home when I'm trying to get chores done or manage daily errands.
Do you also often interrupt others, have trouble waiting your turn, or act impulsively without thinking?

Actually, now that I think about it, I really do struggle with that. I often find myself talking excessively and blurting out answers or interrupting people before they've even finished their sentence. It's something I feel pretty self-conscious about because I just can't seem to stop myself from doing it.

latest_inference.note: Previously the candidates were [Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation), Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Inattentive Presentation)], but the patient now endorses clear hyperactive/impulsive symptoms in addition to inattention: talking excessively, blurting out answers, and interrupting others. That makes the predominantly inattentive presentation unlikely and supports the combined presentation. The symptoms are also longstanding since before age 12 and occur across settings, which further fits ADHD.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient has longstanding symptoms since before age 12 across multiple settings, with clear inattentive features (careless mistakes, poor sustained focus) and hyperactive/impulsive features (restlessness, fidgeting, excessive talking, blurting out answers, interrupting others). This pattern supports ADHD, combined presentation.
